svg.title: The life of one kernel launch
svg.desc: Five CPU steps write into memory the CPU and GPU share, one store rings the doorbell, the GPU reads the ring, the pushbuffer and the launch descriptor, runs the grid and writes a completion marker the CPU polls.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace
Inter, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The life of one kernel launch

text.font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: On the GB10 the CPU and the GPU share one memory, and CUDA++ maps every buffer at the same address on both. Nothing is copied.

svg.text: Blue: the CPU writes. Amber: the GPU acts. Dashed: GPU registers mapped into the process, not memory.

text.font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Measured on the GB10: 24 to 31 µs per extra dependent launch with wait-for-idle (evidence/OWN30B-LAUNCH-COST-20261014T0120Z). Command lists put many launches in one submission.
